clue.text: Strong inclination to write plainsong

parts.note: a pen is the tool used to write, standing for the act
plainsong is a liturgical chant sung in unison

explanation.surface: Someone has a strong urge to compose church music.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a marked liking or taste for something.

clue.text: Exotic fruits prescribed by rules of religious observance

parts.note: PI is crossword shorthand for pious, i.e. religious
laws are rules laid down

explanation.surface: Strange fruit is ordered by the regulations of a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: pilaws are spiced rice dishes of Eastern origin, often studded with dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaw is an Eastern dish of rice, often cooked with dried fruit and spices.

clue.text: Tory mixed up with an oath at tester

indicators.note: mixed up says the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A Conservative gets entangled with someone who witnesses sworn statements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oath at tester' is how the old newspaper text splits attester, someone who witnesses an oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a public official who witnesses and certifies sworn documents.

clue.text: Like Hungary when bereft of a goulash supply

definitions.text: Like Hungary when bereft of a goulash supply

indicators.note: bereft of means robbed of, so a letter is taken out of the country's name

explanation.surface: A nation without its famous stew would go without food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bereft of' removes the A from HUNGARY; the whole clue also describes a starving Hungary, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a food supply leaves people famished.

clue.text: Fame resulting from anything but skill

parts.note: anything but means definitely not
ability is skill or competence

explanation.surface: Celebrity that comes without any talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Notability is the state of being well known or eminent.

clue.text: Fitted-by a bespoke tailor?

parts.note: a made-to-measure tailor fits a customer for a two- or three-piece outfit, and the word also means appropriate

explanation.surface: A garment fitted by a custom tailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Suited means appropriate, and also dressed in a tailored outfit.

clue.text: Rare public tract carrying French article

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
a common is a tract of land open to the public

explanation.surface: An unusual stretch of public land holds an article from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare and uncommon are synonyms meaning seldom found.

clue.text: Deviate from a policy of providing charitable accommodation

definitions.text: Deviate from a policy of providing charitable accommodation

parts.words: Deviate from a policy of providing charitable accommodation
parts.note: the phrase means veer off course, and also describes refusing shelter to someone who asks for it

explanation.surface: A charity drops its policy of housing people.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn away is to swerve aside, and also to refuse admission to someone.

clue.text: Banned bread kneaded by member of the Op

indicators.note: dough is kneaded by working it about, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a left-wing member of the Opposition is called a red

explanation.surface: An opposition politician bakes, and the result is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kneaded' rearranges BREAD into DEBAR; RED is a socialist, here of the Opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Debarred means excluded or prohibited.

clue.text: Among non-churchmen can it be a classical accomplishment of churchmen?

indicators.note: among puts one piece in the midst of the other

parts.note: the laity are people who are not clergy
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Can lay people acquire the old learning that the clergy possess?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to ask whether ordinary people can attain clerical learning; the second word is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Latinity is skill in writing Latin, long the mark of a learned cleric.

clue.text: Seal responsible for mark of wound carried by sailor

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a healed wound
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman bears a scar from an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarab is a beetle-shaped gem used in ancient Egypt as a seal or amulet.

clue.text: Clothes hanger for a decorated RAMC officer?

definitions.text: Clothes hanger for a decorated RAMC officer?

parts.words: Clothes hanger for a decorated RAMC officer?
parts.note: a cupboard for hanging clothes, read as the gown of an army doctor on hospital rounds

explanation.surface: A coat hook for a medal-winning army doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: RAMC is the Royal Army Medical Corps, whose officers work in hospital wards.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a tall cupboard in which clothes are hung.

clue.text: Handicap one thousand and two

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
a pair is two

explanation.surface: A golfer's or racehorse's handicap rated in numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair or handicap is to weaken or hinder.

clue.text: Disguised charm looms perhaps behind her prim pedantic style

definitions.text: perhaps behind her prim pedantic style

indicators.note: disguised means altered in appearance, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hidden charm lurks behind a prudish teacher's manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress of the old prim, fussy type is typically found behind such a manner.

clue.text: Choose to harangue the voters

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
to orate is to speechify at length

explanation.surface: Politicians pick and lecture the public.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of people entitled to vote is the electorate.

clue.text: True copper is packed in a big box

indicators.note: is packed in puts the metal inside the box

parts.note: a crate is a large packing box
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Genuine copper is shipped in a large container.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct, exact or faithful.

clue.text: Not out to make one's name before one gets a badge of office

parts.note: in is the opposite of out, as a batsman is in
to sign is to write one's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone signs and then receives an official emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are emblems showing rank or office.

clue.text: Abandoned and forlorn

explanation.surface: Deserted and wretched.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means both deserted and miserably lonely.

clue.text: Church school one takes on for a meeting of delegates

parts.note: a convent school is run by nuns, a church school
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A church school takes on staff for a conference.
explanation.definitionFit: A convention is a formal assembly of representatives.

clue.text: In the 18th century he held up prince in Piedmontese capital

definitions.text: In the 18th century he held up

indicators.note: in puts one letter inside the city name

parts.note: Turin is the capital of Piedmont in Italy

explanation.surface: An eighteenth-century robber waylays a prince in Turin.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was an English highwayman hanged in 1739; 'held up' means robbed travellers at gunpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Turpin was a notorious English highway robber of the 1730s.

clue.text: Woman taken in by young scout who is a real angel-face

indicators.note: taken in by means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a cub is a junior scout
her is a word referring to a woman

explanation.surface: A lady is fooled by a junior scout with an innocent face.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged child in art, so a sweetly angelic-looking person.

clue.text: Stick to the theme of Adeste Fideles

definitions.meaning: the Latin hymn's opening calls the faithful to come hither, read as AD (to) plus here

explanation.surface: Keep to the subject of the Christmas hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: Adeste Fideles, 'O Come, All Ye Faithful', summons the faithful to be present, which in Latin-English mix reads as 'to here'.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or stay attached, and the hymn's message is 'come to this place'.

clue.text: General Assembly being broadcast, though member states rarely act in it

definitions.text: General Assembly being broadcast, though member states rarely act in it

parts.words: General Assembly being broadcast, though member states rarely act in it
parts.note: a body of nations seldom acting together in concord, read also as a chorus all voicing the same note

explanation.surface: The UN General Assembly is televised, though its nations seldom agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means doing something all together in agreement.

clue.text: Permanently rusticated!

parts.note: rusticated means sent down from university, and also made rural; a field turned over by a plough is rural

explanation.surface: A student sent away from college for good.
explanation.definitionFit: In old university slang to be ploughed was to fail an examination, and farmland is ploughed.

clue.text: Temper shown by young Prince Consort following the dead queen

indicators.note: following places the prince's name after the queen's

parts.note: Queen Anne is dead, as the saying goes
Al is a short name for Albert, Victoria's Prince Consort

explanation.surface: A royal youngster shows a bad temper after a monarch's death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Anne's dead' is an old saying for stale news.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal is to temper metal or glass by heating and slow cooling.

clue.text: Wallet for one dripping with wealth?

definitions.text: Wallet for one dripping with wealth?

parts.words: Wallet for one dripping with wealth?
parts.note: a bulging money-holder, read also as a rich person, since dripping is fat

explanation.surface: A billfold for a very rich person.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-filled money bag, and by extension a wealthy person.

clue.text: Cheered by late edition circulation

indicators.note: circulation suggests going round, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Readers are pleased by the late paper's sales figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means in high spirits, delighted.

clue.text: Friendly, so let it be competent

parts.note: amen means so be it
able means competent

explanation.surface: A pleasant agreement that it may happen, from someone capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable means agreeable and responsive, willing to comply.
